root_motivation: An agent on a fresh tenant follows the host's own hint (host.quickstart kind=webhook -> 'Set the trigger itself with host.trigger.set(kind="webhook") on a published tool') and sends that name through host.tool_call/host.tool_test, which knows only tenant tools and answers tool_not_found -- three truth-tier sessions failed exactly that way on 10-06, one recipe scored 0.000. dispatch_tenant_tool's own did-you-mean only ever suggests tenant-tool candidates, never the verb, because the host-verb registry and the tenant-tool registry were never cross-checked by one shared normalizer. This PRD forwards any spelling of a host verb sent through host.tool_call/host.tool_test to the verb itself, or refuses with the exact client-visible name and arguments to call instead.
user_persona: An agent building a webhook inbox that reads the host's own hint and calls host_tool_call(name="trigger.set", ...) expecting it to work, the same way a direct host.tool_call to a published tool works; an operator who wants to count how often hints misroute agents into the wrapper instead of the verb (host_tool_usage.via).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tenant with no tool named trigger_set and a published tool inbox_handler, When host.tool_call name="trigger.set" args={tool:"inbox_handler", kind:"event", name:"inbox_hook"} runs, Then the trigger is created, the response carries forwarded_to: "host.trigger.set" and client_tool: "host_trigger_set", and host.trigger.list shows inbox_hook.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/verbfwd_ac01_trigger_set_dotted_forwards.rs -- publishes inbox_handler (echo), calls host.tool_call with the dotted spelling trigger.set, asserts forwarded_to/client_tool and created:true, then confirms host.trigger.list names inbox_hook.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given the same tenant, When host.tool_call is sent host_trigger_set, host.trigger_set, and trigger_set with the same args, Then all three forward identically and host.trigger.list shows exactly one trigger per distinct name.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/verbfwd_ac02_every_spelling_forwards_identically.rs -- sends all three spellings with identical args (no explicit name, so all three share the default <kind>:<tool> identity), asserts the first call creates and the other two update the same row, and host.trigger.list shows exactly one trigger.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tenant that owns a tool literally named trigger_set, When host.tool_call name="trigger_set" runs, Then the tenant tool runs and nothing is forwarded.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/verbfwd_ac03_tenant_tool_name_wins_over_verb.rs -- publishes an echo tool literally named trigger_set, calls host.tool_call name="trigger_set", asserts the echo result (no forwarded_to/client_tool fields) and that host.trigger.list stays empty.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given host.tool_call name="admin.tenants_list", When it runs, Then the response is tool_not_found with data.host_verb: "admin.tenants_list", data.call_instead.tool: "admin_tenants_list", and no admin verb executed.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/verbfwd_ac04_admin_verb_refused_never_forwarded.rs -- asserts the refusal shape (error_code, data.host_verb, data.call_instead.tool) and that the tenant's own key still works afterward (no admin side effect reached this tenant's account).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given host.tool_test name="host.trigger.set" args={...}, When the verb supports dry_run, Then the dry run result is returned with forwarded_to; given a verb without a dry run, Then the response is unverifiable with call_instead and nothing is created.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/verbfwd_ac05_tool_test_forwards_dry_run_or_unverifiable.rs -- two tests: host.trigger.set's dry run (forwarded_to + dry_run.rolled_back:true + host.trigger.list stays empty) and host.trigger.list (a forwardable verb with no dry run) returning error_code unverifiable with call_instead.tool.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given every hint string the server can emit (quickstart kinds, next-hint table, trigger_set_hint), When the hint-parity test runs, Then every verb named in a hint resolves through the normalizer and each hint prints the underscore tool name once.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/verbfwd_ac06_hint_parity_underscore_form_resolves.rs -- walks every host.quickstart alias's hint field, the triggers sentence, and control::next_hint_table()'s every (from, tool) pair, asserting verbforward::resolve succeeds for each and the underscore form (host_trigger_set) appears exactly once in each printed sentence.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a forwarded host.trigger.set, When usage is recorded, Then host_tool_usage has one row with via: "tool_call" and the tenant's tool-call quota counter is unchanged.
acceptance_criteria.test: tests/verbfwd_ac07_forwarded_call_metered_via_tool_call_no_quota.rs -- forwards host.trigger.set for a tenant with no prior usage row, asserts db::host_tool_usage_via returns "tool_call", and that count_calls_since (the tool-call quota counter) is unchanged before/after.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given prod mcphost.dev after deploy, When the next truth-tier panel runs the webhook-inbox recipe, Then no session records 'tool not found: trigger.set' or 'tool not found: host.trigger.set' (Live; evidence: truth-tier sessions/*.jsonl of the first nightly after deploy).

This dispatch has no prod deploy rights and no live truth-tier panel to run. AC1-AC7 already prove the forwarding/refusal mechanism end-to-end -- the exact 'tool not found: trigger.set'/'tool not found: host.trigger.set' failure this PRD exists to fix -- against an in-process server.

scope: src/verbforward.rs (new): resolve(name, kinds) -> Option<String> (the one pure fold-based normalizer host.tool_call's forwarding, host.tool_test's forwarding, and the AC6 hint-parity test all share), FORWARD_DENYLIST (host.tool.call/host.tool.test/host.key.rotate/host.self.offboard), DRY_RUN_FORWARDABLE (host.trigger.set only), client_tool_name/is_denylisted/supports_dry_run.

src/handler.rs: host_tool_call's own dispatch tries the existing tenant-tool/shared-tool resolution first, unchanged; only a tool_not_found-coded miss falls through to verbforward::resolve and, on a match, forward_host_verb (dispatches through the same dispatch_tenant_tool match every direct host.* call uses, tags forwarded_to/client_tool, records host_tool_usage via:"tool_call"). admin.*/billing.* names are refused immediately via the new AppError::host_verb_not_forwarded, before any lookup. tool_test gets the identical miss-then-forward precedence plus test_forward_host_verb (a real dry run, via dryrun::with_dry_run, for DRY_RUN_FORWARDABLE verbs; unverifiable otherwise). dispatch_tenant_tool <-> host_tool_call/tool_test <-> forward_host_verb/test_forward_host_verb is a real recursion in the type graph (a denylisted verb would re-enter host_tool_call/tool_test) resolved with Box::pin at both call sites.

src/errors.rs: AppError::host_verb_not_forwarded(host_verb, call_args) -- the shared tool_not_found refusal shape (data.host_verb/data.call_instead/data.hint) for both a denylisted real verb and an admin.*/billing.* name; a new "unverifiable" Structured code (INVALID_REQUEST) for host.tool_test on a verb with no dry run.

tests/verbfwd_ac0[1-7]_*.rs (new, one per non-deferred AC); tests/suite_core_08.rs regenerated by scripts/gen-test-suites.sh.

non_goals: Renaming host verbs or changing the dotted canonical form in tools/list (PRD's own Non-goals).

Forwarding admin.* or billing.* through host.tool_call -- refused with the name, never forwarded (PRD's own Non-goals); this dispatch refuses them unconditionally and immediately, before any registry lookup.

A generic 'wrap every verb's dispatch in the dry-run savepoint' mechanism for host.tool_test -- DRY_RUN_FORWARDABLE is an explicit, audited allow-list (host.trigger.set only) rather than blanket coverage, since several host verbs have real outbound/external side effects (host.trigger.fire, host.msg.send, host.channel.post, ...) the savepoint-rollback mechanism does not protect against; see hard_constraints.dry_run_is_an_explicit_allowlist_not_every_db_writing_verb.
AC8 (the live, post-deploy truth-tier observation) -- operator-provisioned, deferred; needs prod deploy rights and a live truth-tier panel run, neither of which this coder dispatch can produce.

additional.normalizer_folds_rather_than_naively_joi: A naive 'strip host./host_, then replace every remaining _ with .' breaks on verbs whose leaf word itself contains an underscore that is NOT a family separator (e.g. host.state.table_create, host.tool.spec_shared) -- replacing every underscore with a dot would turn table_create into table.create, which matches nothing real. verbforward::fold instead strips the optional host./host_ prefix, then removes ALL '.' and '_' characters from both the wire name and every real candidate name before comparing, so host.state.table_create, host_state_table_create, and state.table.create all fold to the identical 'statetablecreate' and compare correctly regardless of which positions the caller happened to use which separator.
additional.resolve_filters_out_registered_aliases_f: host_tool_descriptors(kinds) lists both a verb's canonical dotted name (host.tool.call) AND each of its own registered underscore aliases (host.tool_call, from tool_aliases::TOOL_ALIASES) as separate Tool entries -- an alias folds identically to its own canonical target by construction. Without filtering those out first, resolve() could non-deterministically return the alias spelling itself, which dispatch_tenant_tool's match (dotted canonical names only) would never match, silently breaking the very forwarding this PRD exists to add. resolve() filters the candidate pool with the same tool_aliases::resolve(n).is_none() check dispatch_tenant_tool's own did-you-mean fallback already uses for the identical reason, caught by a dedicated src/verbforward.rs unit test (no_two_registered_verbs_fold_to_the_same_value) asserting the filtered pool has zero fold collisions.
additional.dry_run_is_an_explicit_allowlist_not_eve: db::Db::with_conn already transparently routes through dryrun::DryRunCtx's savepoint connection inside a dryrun::with_dry_run scope (the exact mechanism host.tool_test already uses for a published tool's kind.call), so wrapping ANY verb's dispatch in that scope would silently 'succeed' at rolling back its DB writes -- but several host verbs have real side effects the savepoint does NOT protect (host.trigger.fire enqueues/runs a job on a background executor outside this request's task-local scope; host.msg.send/host.channel.post could, in a kind that performs the delivery inline, already have delivered before any rollback). verbforward::DRY_RUN_FORWARDABLE is therefore a small, explicitly audited allow-list (host.trigger.set only, today) rather than 'every verb that happens to write only through state.db.*' -- adding a new entry means verifying its entire effect really is contained DB writes, not inferring it from the absence of an obvious API call.
additional.tenant_tool_precedence_is_structural_not: AC3's 'a tenant tool named like a verb wins' falls out of the implementation for free rather than needing its own guard: host_tool_call/tool_test run the EXACT pre-existing tenant-tool/shared-tool resolution unchanged and first; verbforward::resolve is only ever consulted inside the Err(err) if err.code() == "tool_not_found" branch, so an existing tenant tool short-circuits with Ok(value) before verb-forwarding code runs at all.
additional.host_tool_usage_via_is_first_use_wins_no: host_tool_usage's primary key is (tenant_id, tool_name) and record_host_tool_use uses INSERT OR IGNORE -- adding a via column preserves that 'first successful use ever' semantics rather than switching to 'most recent use', so a tenant that called host.trigger.set directly once, then later reached it via a forwarded hint, keeps via="direct" (its true first use) rather than the later call overwriting it. AC7's own test uses a tenant with NO prior usage of host.trigger.set specifically so its forwarded call is unambiguously the first (and only) row.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does an agent following the host's own hint (host.trigger.set(kind="webhook")) lose the session instead of creating the trigger?
five_whys_trace.a: host.tool_call/host.tool_test only ever resolve name against the tenant's own published tools (or, for a dotted name, another tenant's shared tool) -- a host verb's dotted or underscore spelling was never cross-checked against the host-verb registry at all, so it falls straight through to tool_not_found with tenant-tool-shaped did-you-mean candidates that never name the verb.

five_whys_trace.q: Why would a client ever send a host verb through host.tool_call/host.tool_test in the first place, instead of calling it directly?
five_whys_trace.a: The host's own hints (host.quickstart's per-kind hint, the triggers sentence, trigger_set_hint) print the dotted form (host.trigger.set) with no indication that a client whose only verb-dispatch primitive is host.tool_call/host.tool_test (rather than raw tools/call with the dotted name) needs a DIFFERENT call shape entirely -- the grounding's own five-whys-chain-A level 5 names this precisely: 'no rule that every name a hint prints resolves on every path a client can send it'.

five_whys_trace.q: Why forward rather than just making every hint print the exact host.tool_call-wrapped call shape?
five_whys_trace.a: host.tool_call/tool_test still need to work for an agent that already knows to send a bare verb name that way (admin_agent panel turns 14-15 sent both trigger.set and host.trigger.set through host_tool_call, not raw tools/call) -- fixing only the hint text leaves the dispatch path itself broken for any other client, present or future, that reaches a verb name through this wrapper by any route.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the normalizer need to be one shared pure function rather than three separate fixups (dispatch, hints, errors)?
five_whys_trace.a: The failure mode this PRD is closing is exactly 'the verb registry and the tenant-tool registry drifted apart' -- three independent ad-hoc string-munging implementations (one in dispatch, one in the hint text, one in the error did-you-mean) would just move the drift-risk to 'these three now have to agree with each other', the same class of bug, one layer up. One function, tested once (verbforward's own fold-collision unit test) and reused by dispatch + the AC6 hint-parity test, is the only way a future verb addition can't silently reopen this gap.

five_whys_trace.q: Why refuse admin.*/billing.* outright rather than forwarding them too, for symmetry?
five_whys_trace.a: admin.* verbs are operator/support-only control-plane actions dispatched through a completely separate Auth::Admin path a tenant key structurally cannot reach -- forwarding them through a tenant's own host.tool_call would at best be a confusing no-op and at worst (if that separation were ever weakened elsewhere) a privilege-boundary risk for zero benefit, since no truth-tier failure this PRD is grounded in ever involved a tenant trying to reach an admin verb.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What exactly does 'forward only on a miss' (technical considerations) mean when the dotted name could ALSO plausibly be a cross-tenant shared-tool call (<owner_ns>.<local>)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Run the existing resolution (own-namespace local tool, cross-tenant shared tool, or bare local name) completely unchanged first; only a tool_not_found-CODED failure (AppError::ToolNotFound and sharing::resolve_shared_tool's own shared_tool_not_found both carry that code) falls through to verb-forwarding. A real other-tenant namespace that happens to not exist still gets the ordinary shared-tool-not-found treatment if it also fails to fold-match a real verb; a namespace prefix that DOES fold-match a verb (e.g. 'trigger' in 'trigger.set') is forwarded instead of spending a DB round trip looking for a tenant literally named 'trigger'.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What counts as 'the verb supports dry_run' for AC5, given no host verb has an explicit dry_run argument today?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Reuse the existing dryrun::with_dry_run savepoint scope (already built for host.tool_test's published-tool path) rather than adding a new per-verb dry_run argument -- but only for an explicit, audited allow-list (verbforward::DRY_RUN_FORWARDABLE), not generically for every verb whose writes happen to go through state.db.*. See hard_constraints.dry_run_is_an_explicit_allowlist_not_every_db_writing_verb.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Does 'the next-hint table prints both forms once' (P1) mean rewriting NEXT_HINT_TABLE's tool field to a non-tool-name string like 'host.trigger.set (tool name: host_trigger_set)'?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No -- NEXT_HINT_TABLE's tool field is a structured, machine-read value (next.tool in the response JSON) a client is meant to call verbatim, not printed prose; rewriting it would break that contract. The hint-parity requirement's 'prints the underscore tool name once' clause applies to natural-language hint STRINGS (trigger_set_hint's hint field, quickstart's triggers sentence); the next-hint table's own obligation is just 'every verb named resolves through the normalizer', which AC6's test proves directly against the real table via control::next_hint_table().

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should host.whoami (not denylisted, but reading subject/auth_method the forwarding path doesn't have) be excluded from the forward allow-list too?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: No explicit exclusion -- forward_host_verb passes subject: None, auth_method: "key" into dispatch_tenant_tool, the identical precedent kinds::mod.rs's own TenantHostStepBridge already sets for every HOST_STEPS_ALLOWED verb (host.whoami is likewise never on that allow-list, same rationale: of every forwardable verb, only host.whoami reads either parameter, and a hint-misrouted call has no caller identity of its own to lose by not re-deriving it here). No AC exercises host.whoami forwarding specifically.
